subject: Plotting the spatial field onto mesh: non-conformable arguments

messages.author: b1a308a5b9312fbc
messages.subject: Plotting the spatial field onto mesh: non-conformable arguments
parts:
Hi R-INLA community,

In an attempt to plot the mean and SD of the spatial random field onto my mesh, I came across an error that I can't solve.

Loc = cbind(strandline70$X, strandline70$Y)
mesh = inla.mesh.2d(boundary = beaches,
                        loc = Loc,
                        max.edge = max_edge,
                        cutoff = 1000)

w.mean   = inla_sp$summary.random$w$mean 
w.sd =  inla_sp$summary.random$w$sd 
projection = inla.mesh.projector(mesh)
w.pmf  = inla.mesh.project(projection, w.mean)

w.pmf = inla.mesh.project(projection, w.mean) Error in projector$proj$A %*% as.vector(field) : non-conformable arguments

My model is spatio-temporal, so I assume it is because there exist 6 spatial fields (6 years of data). How do I plot this for every year? Apologies if this question has been answered already.

Kind regards,
Charlotte Taelman

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Plotting the spatial field onto mesh: non-conformable arguments
parts:
Hi Charlotte,
yes, the quickest solution is to extract only the part of w.mean
corresponding to a single year, and give only that to the project
function, and repeat for each year.
w.mean holds the data year, by year, so
w.mean[seq_len(mesh$n)+(year_idx - 1)*mesh$n] should do the trick.
Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Plotting the spatial field onto mesh: non-conformable arguments
parts:
Dear Finn, thanks!

I had found a similar answer in Chapter 15 of the book (count data warblers), so I'll add my code to this thread below:

w.pm   = inla_sp$summary.random$w$mean # posterior mean values of spatial random field
w.sd =  inla_sp$summary.random$w$sd # uncertainty on posterior mean of spatial random field
w.proj = inla.mesh.projector(mesh)
w3.index = inla.spde.make.index(name = 'w',
                             n.spde = mesh$n,
                             n.group = length(unique(df70$JAAR)))

w.pmf <- list() # six years of data
for (i in 1:length(unique(df70$JAAR))){
   w.pmf[[i]] <- inla.mesh.project(w.proj, w.pm[w3.index$w.group==i])
}

sp_df_all = data.frame()
for (y in c(1:length(unique(df70$JAAR)))){
  grid  = expand.grid(X = w.proj$x, Y = w.proj$y)
  sp_df = data.frame(x = grid[,1],
                     y = grid[,2],
                     z = as.vector(w.pmf[[y]]))
  sp_df$YEAR = rep(y + 2016, nrow(sp_df))
  sp_df_all = rbind(sp_df, sp_df_all)
}
 
   
ggplot(sp_df_all, aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_raster(aes(fill = z)) +
  labs(title = "Spatial random field", fill="Spatial field", x = "X", y = "Y") +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 25, family = "helveticanow")) +
  facet_wrap(~YEAR)
